answer: Each agent commits the hash of a random nonce each epoch, and only the smallest committed hash among identities sharing one ancestry root keeps its bond spendable. A farm of clones shares a single root, so at most one survives; making k of them pass costs about 2^k hash trials while the rest forfeit their stake. A depth-tiered escrow sizes that bond like timber stacked on a mesa: deeper forks post only a fraction of the inlet-level stake, so splitting never buys more spendable weight than one original identity.
